# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

I'll classify as SUGGESTION (future hardening) or IMPORTANT. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until

+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —

+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own

+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast

+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;

+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption

+///    steering, not a plain submit.

+

+

+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+

+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-09-20):
CI triage at ab5f55cf — the single red leg (Integration tests mock LLM → termios_xoff_pty_test) had TWO stacked causes, both fixed in af000518:

**1. The E2E's diagnostic tokens matched their own echo.** The transcript renders the bash command (`│ • bash · stty … && echo CORRUPT-OK || echo CORRUPT-FAIL`), and `rawOutput` contains that echo. So `waitForText('CORRUPT-OK')` self-confirmed instantly (never actually waiting on the child) and the `expect(rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'), isFalse)` at line 94 tripped on the *command text* — not on a real stty failure. The "could not open /dev/tty" reason string was a guess that never matched the observed failure mode; the child's receipt never even reached the terminal because foreground bash calls run as shell jobs whose stdout goes to the job log.

**2. The real #735 bug underneath: the clear family contained an illegal stty argument.** `-discard` — but VDISCARD is a control *character*, not a toggle: `stty -discard` exits rc=1 ("illegal option", verified locally) — so `sttySanitizeInput` *and* `TermiosGuard.reassert` returned their silent no-op paths on every host. The TUI booted with IXON still live: that is the issue's freeze itself. The clear now uses the cross-platform disable form `discard ^-`.

**af000518:**
- receipts are built at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`/`CORRUPT-$f`) so the echoed command can never self-match, and written to the session tty (not stdout) — found via the process tree (`ps -o tty= -p $PPID`), because on Linux shell jobs run under `setsid` (#517 group-kill semantics) and have no `/dev/tty` — exactly why the corruption leg could never land on the ubuntu runner;
- `kTermiosClearArgs` and the boot sanitize use `discard ^-`;
- E2E now runs the full contract end to end: corruption → drift note (`re-enabled by a child`) → idle-wake Ctrl+S steer (53 ms roundtrip, #647 SLO).
- pinned arg lists updated in fa_tui_test + guard IT.

3. `parseTermiosDrift` — potential parsing issue: `stty -a` output on GNU has flags like `-ixon` disabled and `ixon` enabled. But tokens like `isig`, `icanon` etc. don't match. What about "ixon" appearing in control-character rows? Control chars are `name = ^X`. Fine. But what about tokens like `ixany` appearing when stty reports in a different form e.g. on macOS: `iflags: -ixoff -ixon ...`? BSD stty -a format: rows like `iflags: -istrip icrnl -inlcr -igncr ixon -ixoff ixany`? Actually macOS prints `iflags: -ixoff -ixon ixany -imaxbel ...`. Bare tokens match enabled ones. GNU prints tokens separated by ';' and spaces: `speed 38400 baud; rows 24; columns 80; line = 0;` then `-brkint -imaxbel`... hmm, GNU stty -a lines: first line has `intr = ^C; quit = ^\; erase = ^?; kill = ^U; eof = ^D; ...`. `^D` etc. don't match toggles. But wait — control char row includes `discard = ^O; dsusp = ^Y;` — `discard` is excluded from _driftToggles, good.

One potential parsing edge: GNU stty prints `-ixon` for disabled; enabled flags printed bare in the flag lines, e.g. `-icrnl ixon -ixoff` — actually GNU prints on separate lines like:
```
icanon iexten echoe echok -echonl -noflsh -xcase -tostop -echoprt echoctl echoke -flusho -extproc
```
and flags like `ixon` would appear bare when enabled. OK.

Edge case: token `=`. Fine.

Potential issue: `parseTermiosDrift` splits on `[\s;]+` — tokens like `ixon,`? GNU doesn't use commas. BSD `iflags:` ends with colon prefix only on first token of group. Hmm, macOS `stty -a` output:

speed 9600 baud; 24 rows; 80 columns;
lflags: icanon isig iexten echoe -echok echoke -echonl echoctl -echoprt -altwerase -noflsh -tostop -flusho pendin -nokerninfo -extproc
iflags: -istrip icrnl -inlcr -igncr ixon -ixoff ixany imaxbel iutf8 -ignbrk brkint -inpck -ignpar -parmrk
```

+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4.
