@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

Possibly yes (dart_tui may use WinConsole). If TUI runs on Windows, each tool phase spawns stty → exception swallowed. Minor perf/noise. SUGGESTION. Inline at agent_cli.dart:657.

4. **SUGGESTION**: `/termios` fallback message "no tty available (stty missing or no /dev/tty)" in line mode is slightly misleading — line mode may have a tty; the guard just doesn't own it. Trivial. Maybe fold into general comment instead. The line is in diff (agent_cli_commands.dart:213). SUGGESTION inline. Hmm — keep the review focused; this is minor. I'll include as a small suggestion inline.

5. Windows: also `Platform.isWindows` unused in agent_cli.dart? Not relevant.

Is there any BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? Let me think hard about correctness:

- `attachTermiosGuard` ordering: guard runs before prior hook. The prior hook (phase labels) calls `_pushBusyPhase(null)`? Order fine.

- Race: afterToolCall is invoked per tool call; if two tool calls run in parallel (parallel tool calls supported?), two reasserts run concurrently — both probe/clear the same tty; benign (stty clear is idempotent). Two concurrent `stty -F /dev/tty` calls are fine.

- `reassert` clear fails → returns checked:false and doesn't report drift — flags stay drifted until next tool call. Acceptable.

- The guard awaits `Process.run` — could hang if stty hangs? stty -a on a tty doesn't hang. No timeout, but Process.run on a tty probe is quick. A missing timeout is listed in guidelines' performance dimension... `stty -a </dev/tty` — note: probe does NOT redirect stdin from /dev/tty; it uses `-F /dev/tty` device flag, so no stdin interaction. Won't block. Fine.

- E2E test: `ps -o tty= -p $PPID | xargs` — on the CI runner, `$PPID` is the shell-job's parent... they explained setsid. Works per author (2× green). Fine.

- Test `_FakeTty.runner` mutates enabled for any arg starting with '-': for the clear list `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl discard ^- -ixany` it removes all. Good.

- One more: in `TermiosGuard` default hasTerminal `_realHasTerminal` is kept for other potential users; AgentCli overrides. Fine.

- `kTermiosClearArgs` is `List<String>` const; spread in const context? Used in non-const list literals — fine.

- Coverage: drift note in line mode — no probes, so no bogus notes. ✅

- `_printTermiosDump` in TUI mode on Windows: dumpSettings → stty missing → ProcessException caught → null → hint. ✅

Anything about the hidden `/termios` not in slash menu — cli_parity test classifies it. ✅

Documentation: AGENTS.md mentions docs? Not needed.

One more possible IMPORTANT: in `agent_cli.dart` the guard is created with `runner: config.sttyRunner` — in production null → `_processStty`. But the boot sanitize in FaTuiController uses `config.sttyRunner` too. Consistent. ✅

What about `hasTerminal: () => _useTui` — with an injected runner in TUI tests, `_useTui` must be true; the IT passes useTui:true with TuiProgramHooks, and FakeCliIO.supportsRawMode presumably true. ✅ (tests pass).

Background jobs completing (e.g. a curses app restoring termios on exit while backgrounded) can re-corrupt. But the same freeze existed pre-PR in all cases; this PR strictly improves. The gap is a scope limitation, documented implicitly ("after every foreground tool phase"). I'll make it a SUGGESTION with clear reasoning.

Also the duplicate import — check whether `directives_ordering` or any custom static gate checks import uniqueness... They have "static gates" (scripts/). Let me quickly grep scripts for a gate on duplicate imports? Probably not. Skip — tests/gates pass per author.

Actually, let me double check one thing: does the repo have a custom size/gate script that would count termios_guard lines etc.? agent_cli.dart is 2743 < 2800 ✅.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). # pr-738: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable

## Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the ownership gate drops the Windows guard that `TermiosGuard`'s own default keeps**

`TermiosGuard._realHasTerminal` is `!Platform.isWindows && stdin.hasTerminal`, but the override here is `hasTerminal: () => _useTui`. On a Windows host where the TUI does boot (`stdin.hasTerminal && _rawModeOk` can both be true under Windows Terminal), every tool phase will attempt `Process.run('stty', ...)`, which throws `ProcessException` — swallowed by contract, so functionally harmless, but it's a doomed spawn + exception per tool call for the whole session. The boot sanitize kept its `Platform.isWindows` gate in `_sanitizeTermiosInput`, so the guard is the only path that lost it.

```dart
_termiosGuard = TermiosGuard(
  runner: config.sttyRunner,
  hasTerminal: () => _useTui && !Platform.isWindows,
);
```

(With an injected `sttyRunner` tests bypass the real-host gates anyway, so the IT legs are unaffected.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: residual gap — background shell jobs can re-corrupt the tty after the last probe**

The guard re-asserts only at *foreground* after-tool boundaries. But the bash tool yields slow commands to background (`ShellJobRegistry`), and a backgrounded child — a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit, an `stty ixon` in a detached script — can flip IXON **after** the final probe of the turn. The #735 freeze then stays live until the *next* tool call clears it, with no drift note and no protection in between. The PTY E2E was explicitly redesigned around this race (fast corruptor inside the foreground grace), which confirms the window is real.

Not a blocker — the issue's recipe is the foreground case and this PR strictly improves on main — but worth a follow-up: re-assert on shell-job completion (`ShellJobRegistry` already tracks lifecycle), or at minimum document the residual window in the `termios_guard.dart` library doc so the next triager doesn't chase it.

💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate import of the same library — merge the two `show`s**

`termios_guard.dart` is imported twice in this file (line 14 `show kTermiosClearArgs`, and here `show SttyRunner`). Legal Dart and no lint fires, but one import reads better and matches how every other multi-symbol import in this block is written:

```dart
import 'termios_guard.dart' show SttyRunner, kTermiosClearArgs;
```

💡 **SUGGESTION: the `/termios` fallback message is misleading in line mode**

In interactive line mode (and `fa -p` from a terminal) there usually **is** a tty — the guard just doesn't own raw mode on it (`hasTerminal: () => _useTui` returns false by design), so `dumpSettings()` is null and the user reads "no tty available (stty missing or no /dev/tty)", which sends triage in the wrong direction. Since this command exists precisely for freeze triage, naming the real reason helps:

```dart
io.writeln(
  dump ??
      'termios dump unavailable (not in TUI mode, stty missing, or no /dev/tty)',
);
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(

+            'error',
+      );

+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');

+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 738
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/738
- **Title**: fix(735): TermiosGuard — re-assert raw-mode tty flags after tool phases so Ctrl+S steering survives IXON re-enable
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/735-xoff-freeze` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +1171
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-09-20T11:15:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-21T01:39:47Z

## PR Description

Fixes #735

## Root cause (per the issue's RCA, confirmed by the repro)

`sttySanitizeInput` clears `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/discard` **once at TUI boot** and never re-asserts. Any tool child sharing the session tty (pager, ssh, python termios, a curses app restoring its saved termios, `stty` itself) can re-enable IXON mid-session. With IXON on, Ctrl+S (0x13) is the tty driver's VSTOP byte: the kernel eats it, output suspends, any key resumes it (IXANY) — steering dies while fa never sees the byte.

## Delivered

- **TermiosGuard** (`lib/src/cli/termios_guard.dart`): after every foreground tool phase (composed onto `Agent.afterToolCall`, the same seam `attachToolPhaseLabels` uses) probes `stty -a`; when any of `ixon/ixoff/icrnl/ixany` is back on, re-clears the whole family `-ixon -ixoff -icrnl -discard -ixany`. Injectable runner seam identical in spirit to `sttySanitizeInput`'s; no tty / missing stty / failed probe = silent no-op that never breaks the turn (wrap-and-swallow in the hook).
- **Observability**: when a re-assert actually changes flags, one dim transcript note names the drift ("tty: ixon, ixany re-enabled by a child process — cleared (Ctrl+S steering safe)") — the trail that identifies which child corrupts the tty. Plus a hidden `/termios` command dumping live `stty -a` (not in the slash menu).
- **Belt-and-braces**: boot sanitize now also clears `-ixany`; the guard's clear list matches.
- **Seam**: `AgentCliConfig.sttyRunner` routes both the TUI boot sanitize and the guard through one injectable runner (tests model the tty headlessly); `FaTuiController` takes it as an optional ctor param. Production path unchanged (real `stty`; guard no-ops without a terminal, so headless/line hosts are untouched).
- **Steering binding unchanged** — once 0x13 reaches fa, the #647 path delivers ≤2s. No changes to Ctrl+S handling.

## Tests (TDD: UT+IT red first, then green; wiring-red proven by disabling the attach)

- **UT** `test/cli/termios_guard_test.dart` — state-machine stty runner: drift detected + cleared + named; no drift = single probe (no spam); ProcessException / failed probe / headless = silent no-op without a single spawn; `discard = ^O` control-char row never reads as drift; `attachTermiosGuard` wraps afterToolCall preserving prior hooks; guard failure never breaks the tool phase.
- **IT** `test/cli/agent_cli_termios_guard_test.dart` — full AgentCli boot in TUI mode, headless: boot sanitize through the injected runner → bash tool phase corrupts the simulated tty → guard re-asserts at the after-tool boundary (event-order assert: clear issued before the steer keys) → drift note on the transcript → `0x13` steers into the running agent (second model turn contains `[steering from user] steer me`).
- **E2E PTY** `test/integration/termios_xoff_pty_test.dart` — the issue's deterministic recipe: `stty ixon ixany < /dev/tty` via the bash tool mid-run, then queued message + Ctrl+S → asserts the drift note, the `pending` panel (byte reached fa), `delivered` at the boundary, and the model's STEERED-ACK. **This leg runs in CI only** — the local lane sandbox denies `openpty` (all pre-existing PTY suites fail locally with the same denial; verified against `ssh_shift_gate_test.dart`).
- **REG green locally**: `agent_cli_steering_slo_test` + `msg_slo_delivery_test` (#647 AC1–AC4), `shift_hid_test` + `fa_tui_test` (#77 wire matrix, sanitize args updated for `-ixany`), `agent_cli_test`, `agent_cli_busy_steering_test`, `tool_phase_labels_test`, TUI adapter/socket/mouse/overlay suites, `slash_menu`/`queue`/`tools` command suites — 200+ tests, all passing.

## Remaining (out of scope, per the issue's lean)

- No second steering key binding (e.g. Ctrl+T survival path) — guard first, revisit only if hosts without `stty` keep biting (issue's open question).
- `dart analyze`: the lane sandbox hangs the CLI analyzer (syscall-level canonicalize denial); per-file analysis-server diagnostics are clean on every touched file except one provably-stale cross-checkout false positive (the shared analysis server resolves the worktree against the main checkout's pre-change `fa_tui.dart`; the full-package compile via the test runs above is the authoritative check). Zero new lint introduced by the diff — formatted with `dart format`.

## Local-lane environment notes (not part of the diff)

The sandbox also denies the sqlite3 build-hook's path canonicalization, so local `flutter test` runs used a temporary, uncommitted pubspec-overrides redirect of sqlite3 to a hook-less local copy (system libsqlite3 fallback). Nothing of this ships: the PR contains only the nine intended files.

@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+@TestOn('vm')
+@Tags(['integration'])
+@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))
+/// Issue #735 E2E: a child re-enables tty IXON mid-session, so Ctrl+S
+/// (0x13) is eaten by the line discipline as XOFF — output freezes until
+/// any key (IXANY) and steering never reaches fa. The TermiosGuard must
+/// re-assert the raw-mode input flags after every foreground tool phase,
+/// keeping the Ctrl+S steer path alive.
+///
+/// Deterministic recipe (CI-stable redesign after the first leg flaked —
+/// the bash tool yields slow commands to background, so probe timing
+/// must never race a still-running child):
+/// 1. a FAST bash tool call corrupts the session tty and writes its own
+///    receipt (`CORRUPT-OK`) to that tty — it completes inside the
+///    foreground grace, so the after-tool boundary (the guard's probe) is
+///    strictly AFTER the corruption; the receipt doubles as a fail-fast
+///    diagnostic (CORRUPT-FAIL) if the child cannot reach the session tty.
+///    Both receipts are runtime-built (`CORRUPT-$o`) so the transcript's
+///    own echo of the command can never match the test's waits;
+/// 2. the drift note names the flags the guard cleared;
+/// 3. after the turn settles, a typed message + Ctrl+S (0x13) steers as
+///    an idle wake turn — proving the byte reached fa post-corruption
+///    (pre-fix it freezes output instead) and was interpreted as
+///    steering, not a plain submit.
+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+import 'package:fa_llm_mock/fa_llm_mock.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+import 'pty_harness.dart';
+
+void main() {
+  test(
+    'Ctrl+S still steers after a child re-enables IXON mid-session '
+    '(issue #735)',
+    timeout: const Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5)),
+    () async {
+      final tempHome = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_xoff_pty_');
+      final projectDir = '${tempHome.path}/project';
+      Directory(projectDir).createSync(recursive: true);
+      File('${tempHome.path}/.fah/config.yaml')
+        ..createSync(recursive: true)
+        ..writeAsStringSync('''
+provider: openai-completions
+model: mock-model
+mode: code
+approvalMode: yolo
+allowedTools: []
+''');
+      addTearDown(() => tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true));
+
+      final server = await MockLlmServer.start();
+      addTearDown(server.stop);
+      // Turn 1: corrupt the tty exactly like a real child would (a pager,
+      // ssh, or a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit). The
+      // command is FAST — it completes before the tool's yield grace, so
+      // the guard's after-tool probe lands strictly after it.
+      // The bash tool runs foreground commands as shell jobs, and on Linux
+      // jobs start under `setsid` (issue #517 group-kill semantics) — the
+      // child has NO controlling terminal, so `< /dev/tty` fails there
+      // while working on setsid-less macOS. A real misbehaving child can
+      // find the session tty through the process tree, so the corruptor
+      // does exactly that; the receipt is written to that tty (NOT stdout,
+      // which the job log captures) so it lands in the PTY stream.
+      // Receipt tokens are BUILT at runtime (`CORRUPT-$o`) — the literal
+      // text must never appear inside the command string, because the TUI
+      // echoes the command into the transcript and `rawOutput` contains
+      // that echo: a literal token would self-confirm the wait and
+      // self-trip the failure guard before the child even ran.
+      server.enqueueToolCall(
+        'bash',
+        '{"command": "o=OK; f=FAIL; t=/dev/\$(ps -o tty= -p \$PPID | xargs); '
+            'if stty ixon ixany < \$t; then echo CORRUPT-\$o > \$t; '
+            'else echo CORRUPT-\$f > \$t; fi"}',
+      );
+      server.enqueueText('TURN-SETTLED');
+      server.enqueueText('IDLE-STEER-ACK');
+
+      final harness = await FaCliHarness.spawn(
+        workingDirectory: projectDir,
+        extraEnv: {'HOME': tempHome.path, 'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'mock'},
+        args: [
+          '--provider',
+          'openai-completions',
+          '--base-url',
+          server.baseUrl,
+          '--model',
+          'mock-model',
+          '--session',
+          'xoff-pty',
+        ],
+      );
+      addTearDown(harness.close);
+      await harness.waitForBoot(timeout: const Duration(seconds: 300));
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('run the tool please');
+      // The corruption's own receipt — and a fail-fast diagnostic: if the
+      // corrupting child cannot reach the session tty (e.g. no tty in the
+      // process tree), CORRUPT-FAIL names the gap instead of leaving a
+      // mystery timeout on the drift note below.
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'CORRUPT-OK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      expect(
+        harness.rawOutput.contains('CORRUPT-FAIL'),
+        isFalse,
+        reason:
+            'the corrupting child could not reach the session tty — '
+            'see the bash job card in rawOutput for the child\'s stty '
+            'error',
+      );
+
+      // Observability contract: the guard names the drift it cleared
+      // (the probe ran at the after-tool boundary, strictly after the
+      // child finished corrupting).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        're-enabled by a child',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
+      );
+
+      // Let the turn settle — the idle-steer wake below starts a fresh
+      // turn (deterministic: no mid-run race against the yield grace).
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'TURN-SETTLED',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+
+      // The steer gesture itself: with IXON back on (pre-fix), this byte
+      // is swallowed by the tty as XOFF — output freezes and nothing
+      // reaches fa. Post-fix the guard already re-cleared the flags, so
+      // 0x13 arrives, is interpreted as STEERING (not a plain submit),
+      // and the idle wake turn answers.
+      harness.sendText('steer me please');
+      final sw = Stopwatch()..start();
+      harness.sendCtrlS();
+      await harness.waitForText(
+        'IDLE-STEER-ACK',
+        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
+      );
+      // ignore: avoid_print
+      print('STEER-ROUNDTRIP ${sw.elapsedMilliseconds}ms');
+
+      await harness.runSlashCommand('/exit');
+      await harness.close();
+    },
+  );
+}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: residual gap — background shell jobs can re-corrupt the tty after the last probe**

The guard re-asserts only at *foreground* after-tool boundaries. But the bash tool yields slow commands to background (`ShellJobRegistry`), and a backgrounded child — a curses app restoring its saved termios on exit, an `stty ixon` in a detached script — can flip IXON **after** the final probe of the turn. The #735 freeze then stays live until the *next* tool call clears it, with no drift note and no protection in between. The PTY E2E was explicitly redesigned around this race (fast corruptor inside the foreground grace), which confirms the window is real.

Not a blocker — the issue's recipe is the foreground case and this PR strictly improves on main — but worth a follow-up: re-assert on shell-job completion (`ShellJobRegistry` already tracks lifecycle), or at minimum document the residual window in the `termios_guard.dart` library doc so the next triager doesn't chase it.
"}
